plan.title: Plate Tectonics: A Moving Planet
plan.hook: The ground under every city is a raft in slow motion. The rafts are thicker than the crust alone, they grind along three kinds of edges, and the friction on those edges is why earthquakes arrive as sudden releases of centuries of patience.
objectives: State what a lithospheric plate includes and what the plates move over
Classify a boundary as divergent, convergent, or transform from the relative motion of its plates
Explain how stress builds and releases in an earthquake, and why P waves outrun S waves

sections.heading: The moving pieces include more than crust
points: Lithospheric plates include crust and the rigid uppermost mantle

points: Divergent boundaries pull apart; convergent boundaries push together; transform boundaries slide past

points: Stress builds along faults until rock slips, releasing the loading suddenly

sections.heading: The moving pieces include more than crust
sections.body: Lithospheric plates include crust and the rigid uppermost mantle. They move slowly over the deeper mantle.
sections.visual: Plates are rigid pieces of lithosphere that ride over the deeper mantle. Highlight each plate to see that the moving unit is thicker than the crust alone.

questions.q: What exactly is a plate made of?
questions.hint: It is more than the crust — what rides along with it?
questions.answer: A lithospheric plate includes the crust and the rigid uppermost mantle. The moving pieces are thicker than the crust alone, and they move slowly over the deeper mantle.

questions.hint: Name the layer beneath the lithosphere as the section describes it.
questions.answer: The deeper mantle. Plates are rigid pieces of lithosphere that ride over it.

sections.heading: Pull apart, push together, slide past
sections.body: Divergent boundaries pull apart, convergent boundaries push together, transform boundaries slide past.
sections.visual: Three relative motions: plates separate, collide, or slide past. The boundary type is about direction of motion, not how dramatic the landscape looks.
sections.diagram: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Three boundary types"><title>Three boundary types</title><rect x="0" y="0" width="800" height="400" rx="16" fill="#101923"/><text x="28" y="35" fill="#e8ecf1" font-size="21" font-family="sans-serif">Pull apart · push together · slide past</text><path d="M28 51 L772 51" fill="none" stroke="#344253" stroke-width="2"/><g class="lw-step"><text x="140" y="160" fill="#7cc7ff" font-size="18" text-anchor="middle">Divergent</text><path d="M80 220 L120 220" stroke="#7cc7ff" stroke-width="3" fill="none" class="lw-flow"/><path d="M160 220 L200 220" stroke="#7cc7ff" stroke-width="3" fill="none" class="lw-flow"/></g><g class="lw-step"><text x="400" y="160" fill="#7ee2a8" font-size="18" text-anchor="middle">Convergent</text><path d="M340 220 L380 220" stroke="#7ee2a8" stroke-width="3" fill="none"/><path d="M420 220 L460 220" stroke="#7ee2a8" stroke-width="3" fill="none"/></g><g class="lw-step"><text x="640" y="160" fill="#ffd479" font-size="18" text-anchor="middle">Transform</text><path d="M580 200 L700 200" stroke="#ffd479" stroke-width="3" fill="none"/></g><path d="M28 350 L772 350" fill="none" stroke="#344253" stroke-width="2"/><text x="28" y="379" fill="#9aa6b8" font-size="15">Boundary type sets the relative motion</text></svg>

questions.q: Name the three boundary types and the motion at each.
questions.hint: The heading lists them as three everyday verbs.
questions.answer: Divergent boundaries pull apart, convergent boundaries push together, and transform boundaries slide past one another.

questions.q: A boundary has modest scenery but plates sliding sideways. What type is it?
questions.hint: Classify by motion, not by landscape.
questions.answer: A transform boundary. The boundary type is about the direction of relative motion, not how dramatic the landscape looks.

sections.heading: Slow loading can release suddenly
sections.body: Stress builds along faults until rock slips. P waves travel faster than S waves from the focus.
sections.visual: From the focus, compressional P waves expand faster than shear S waves. Scrub the motion: the cyan P front stays ahead of the purple S front — that lag is the teaching point.

questions.q: Why does an earthquake release energy suddenly rather than gradually?
questions.hint: The heading pairs slow loading with sudden release — what gives way?
questions.answer: Stress builds along a fault while the rock holds; when the rock slips, the accumulated loading releases at once. Slow loading, sudden release.

questions.q: Which seismic wave arrives first from the focus, and why?
questions.hint: Compare the two wave types the section names.
questions.answer: The P wave. P waves are compressional and travel faster than the shear S waves, so the P front stays ahead of the S front.

choices: Crust only
Crust plus the rigid uppermost mantle
The whole mantle plus crust
Mantle only, sliding under a fixed crust
questions.explain: The plates include crust and the rigid uppermost mantle — the moving unit is thicker than the crust alone — and they move slowly over the deeper mantle.

choices: Quickly, at speeds you could watch
Only during earthquakes
Slowly, over the deeper mantle
Only where oceans cover them
questions.explain: The section describes rigid lithospheric plates moving slowly over the deeper mantle; earthquakes are releases along their boundaries, not the moments when motion happens.

questions.q: Two plates are pulling apart at their shared edge. The boundary is…
choices: Convergent
Transform
Divergent
A fault with no classification
questions.explain: Divergent boundaries pull apart. Convergent boundaries push together, and transform boundaries slide past.

questions.q: The right way to classify a boundary is by…
choices: How mountainous the landscape is
The direction of the plates' relative motion
How many earthquakes it produces
Whether it lies under an ocean
questions.explain: The visual states it: the boundary type is about direction of motion, not how dramatic the landscape looks.

questions.q: At a fault, an earthquake happens when…
choices: Stress builds until the rock slips and releases it
The plates stop moving for good
P waves overtake S waves
The mantle pushes the plates apart
questions.explain: Stress builds along faults until rock slips; the slow loading is released suddenly. The waves are the consequence that radiates from the focus, not the cause.

questions.q: From the focus, the P front stays ahead of the S front because…
choices: P waves start earlier at the focus
P waves are compressional and travel faster than the shear S waves
S waves slow down in the mantle
P waves take a shorter path
questions.explain: Both wave types leave the focus together; the compressional P waves simply travel faster than the shear S waves, so the cyan P front stays ahead.

sections.title: More than crust is moving
bullets: A plate = crust + rigid uppermost mantle (the lithosphere).
The moving unit is thicker than the crust alone.
Plates move slowly over the deeper mantle.
sections.notes: The word "plate" undersells the thickness. Each moving piece is a slab of lithosphere — crust welded to the rigid top of the mantle — rafting over the deeper mantle below.
sections.visual: Plates are rigid pieces of lithosphere that ride over the deeper mantle. Highlight each plate to see that the moving unit is thicker than the crust alone.

sections.title: Three motions, three boundaries
bullets: Classify by direction of motion, not by scenery.
sections.notes: Every boundary is one of three relative motions. Learn to read the arrows and the label follows — a quiet landscape can sit on any of the three.
sections.visual: Three relative motions: plates separate, collide, or slide past. The boundary type is about direction of motion, not how dramatic the landscape looks.

sections.title: Slow loading, sudden release
bullets: Stress builds along faults while rock holds.
When rock slips, the loading releases at once.
P waves (compressional, faster) outrun S waves (shear, slower).
sections.notes: An earthquake is a slip, not an explosion: stress accumulates silently, then the fault lets go. The two wave types then race outward, and the faster compressional P wave always leads.
sections.visual: From the focus, compressional P waves expand faster than shear S waves. Scrub the motion: the cyan P front stays ahead of the purple S front — that lag is the teaching point.

enrichment.audioTitle: Plate Tectonics: A Moving Planet — a conversation

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.line: Quick test of the first idea: when we say a plate moves, what is the thing that is moving?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.line: More than that. A lithospheric plate includes the crust and the rigid uppermost mantle — the moving unit is thicker than the crust alone. What does it move over?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.line: Good. Now boundaries. Three kinds — give me the motion at each.

turns.speaker: student
turns.line: Divergent pull apart, convergent push together, transform slide past.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.line: And if a boundary looks scenic and dramatic, does that tell you its type?

turns.speaker: student
turns.line: No — the visual warned about that. Type is about direction of motion, not how dramatic the landscape looks.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.line: Exactly. Last part: a fault is quiet for two hundred years, then produces an earthquake in seconds. Where was the energy in the quiet years?

turns.speaker: student
turns.line: Building as stress along the fault while the rock held — then the rock slipped and released it.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.line: Slow loading, sudden release. The slip radiates waves: which arrives first at a distant station, P or S, and why?

turns.speaker: student
turns.line: P — it is compressional and travels faster than the shear S wave, so its front stays ahead.

turns.speaker: student
turns.line: And both waves leave the focus at the same moment — the lag is purely the speed difference?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.line: Just so. Scrub the diagram's motion and the cyan P front stays ahead of the purple S front the whole way out; nothing but their speeds separates them.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.line: That is the whole course: thick plates, three motions, and one lag between two wavefronts that proves which is faster.

nodes.note: Each name matches one direction of relative motion.
